description: FIND-201's resolution (REQ-101's new filterProductiveCitizens join, REQ-305/REQ-402's 'set active_since'/'flip status in that SAME ledger.js row') is built on an assumed keyed/mutable-row abstraction that the real, cited ledger.js does not have and that the spec itself commits to leaving UNMODIFIED. ledger.js exports exactly two functions: readChildren (parses every line, returns them all, unfiltered, undeduplicated) and appendChild (raw JSONL append, no key, no upsert). There is no update-by-child_id, no upsert, no 'find and mutate the row for this child_id' primitive anywhere in the file or its own test suite (__tests__/ledger.test.js only ever exercises DISTINCT child_ids per row; it never tests two rows sharing one child_id). Yet REQ-305 requires 'in that SAME ledger.js row, ALSO set a new field active_since' when a child transitions provisioning->active, and REQ-402 requires flipping status 'in that SAME ledger row' from active->bootstrap_failed (and back, per its own retroactive-correction edge case). Given ledger.js is append-only, the only way to record either transition is to APPEND A NEW LINE with the same child_id -- meaning a single child_id will legitimately have MULTIPLE ledger rows over its lifecycle (provisioning, then active, possibly later bootstrap_failed, possibly later corrected back to active). This exact multi-row-per-child_id pattern is independently confirmed as the REAL, already-established convention in this codebase: the superseded run.sh (lines 124-140, 200-220) appends a 'provisioning' row, then LATER appends a SECOND row with the SAME child_id and an updated status (seed_failed or active) for every single real spawn attempt -- proving readChildren's raw output routinely contains duplicate child_id rows in production usage. Neither REQ-101's filterProductiveCitizens contract, REQ-101's Acceptance Criteria, nor PROP-101d's fixture description ever specifies how to reconcile multiple ledgerRows entries sharing one child_id into 'the' row a citizen is matched against -- PROP-101d's own fixture assumes exactly one row per test citizen, never testing the duplicate-id case. This is precisely the ambiguity the iteration-4 manifest asked to be checked ('what happens with duplicate child_id matches') and it is unresolved: an implementation could take the FIRST row per child_id (meaning a child would NEVER be observed as active/bootstrap_failed by filterProductiveCitizens, since its first-ever row is always 'provisioning'), the LAST row (the only correct reading, but never specified), or something nondeterministic -- and no test in this spec's own acceptance criteria would catch the wrong choice, since PROP-101d never exercises >1 row per id.

evidence.snippet: test("appendChild is append-only (preserves prior rows)", () => { ... appendChild(f, { child_id: "anicca-c001" }); appendChild(f, { child_id: "anicca-c002" }); ... }); // never tests the SAME child_id appended twice

appendChild(...) writes a 'provisioning' ROW (line 137-140), then a LATER, SEPARATE appendChild call writes a SECOND row with the SAME child_id and status:'seed_failed' (200-205) OR status:'active' (213-220) -- proving duplicate-child_id rows are the real, existing runtime behavior this ledger already produces

'a citizen WITH a matching ledger row is EXCLUDED if that row's status is...' (singular 'that row'); 'in that SAME ledger.js row, ALSO set a new field active_since'; 'flips exactly those past the window to "bootstrap_failed" in that SAME ledger row'

"Effectful Shell (existing, reused unmodified) + new registry-append side effect" | "~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/ledger.js::appendChild/readChildren" | "EFFECTFUL (existing)" | "Append-only JSONL; already implemented, unmodified."
